page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 20 shared vCPUs and a system memory capacity of 256.0 GB, yielding 12.8 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with three NVIDIA L4 graphics processing units based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM.

This configuration does not include local storage, meaning external storage volumes must be attached to host operating systems and application data. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the 20 vCPUs are allocated on a shared basis, CPU-bound workloads may experience resource contention compared to dedicated-core instances, representing a key architectural tradeoff for this hardware profile.

Given the presence of three NVIDIA L4 GPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, this server is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. It is suited for machine learning inference, data science pipelines, video transcoding, and parallel computing tasks that require significant VRAM but can tolerate shared CPU resources. The shared CPU allocation offers a more cost-efficient entry point for multi-GPU acceleration compared to dedicated bare-metal or high-end compute instances.
